description: Machine-readable inventory of React audit checks: toolchain and lint, effects and custom hooks, state, and components and server boundaries.

statusTaxonomy.partial: The invariant mostly holds, with exceptions, or a soft check shows mixed adherence.
statusTaxonomy.violation: Concrete code or configuration breaks the invariant.

relatedAudits.relationship: Owns where server data loads, the client-state strategy, and module-level state ownership; this audit judges state inside component trees.
Owns secrets and private fields reaching the browser; this audit rates the server-client module graph and prop serialisability.
Owns linter configuration quality; this audit owns whether the React hooks rules apply to component files.
Owns memoization and rendering cost; this audit owns effect correctness.
Owns error boundaries and request error paths; this audit owns effect cleanup and race handling.

checks.title: Hooks lint rules enforced for component files
checks.rationale: Without the hooks rules, conditional hooks, stale effect dependencies, and impure renders reach production unchecked, and the React Compiler silently skips the components that break its rules.
checks.expectation: eslint-plugin-react-hooks 7's `recommended` configuration (rules-of-hooks, exhaustive-deps, and the React Compiler rules) applies to every component and hook file, read statically from the ESLint configuration; Biome's two hook rules count as partial.
checks.violationSignal: No hook rule applies to component files (missing), or the classic rules are on without the compiler rules, or some rules are off for some files (partial).

checks.title: Built with a maintained toolchain
checks.rationale: Create React App was deprecated in February 2025, so its build stack gets no fixes and its dependency tree keeps known vulnerabilities.
checks.expectation: No package builds with Create React App (`react-scripts`, alone or wrapped by CRACO or react-app-rewired); apps use a framework or a maintained build tool such as Vite.

checks.title: Exhaustive-deps suppressions are justified
checks.rationale: An unexplained exhaustive-deps suppression hides a stale value inside an effect, the bug the rule exists to catch.
checks.expectation: Every `react-hooks/exhaustive-deps` suppression (or Biome `useExhaustiveDependencies` ignore) gives its reason after ` -- ` or in an adjacent comment.

checks.title: Effects do not derive or mirror state
checks.rationale: An effect that copies props or state into other state renders a stale value first and drifts when a dependency is missed, the commonest effect bug React's documentation warns about.
checks.expectation: Values computed from props or state are computed during render; state that must reset when a prop changes uses a `key`; event logic runs in event handlers, not in effects that watch state; parents are notified from the event, not from an effect.
checks.violationSignal: An effect whose only work is calling a state setter with values derived from props or state, an effect chain, or an effect that calls a parent callback when state changes.

checks.title: Effects clean up and ignore stale results
checks.rationale: An effect without cleanup leaks subscriptions and timers, and a fetch without an abort or ignore flag lets an older response overwrite a newer one.
checks.expectation: Every effect that subscribes, listens, starts a timer, or starts async work returns a cleanup that unsubscribes, clears, aborts, or sets an ignore flag; external stores are read with `useSyncExternalStore`.
checks.violationSignal: A fetch or other async call in an effect with no abort or ignore flag, or a listener, subscription, interval, or observer with no cleanup.

checks.title: Effect dependencies are honest
checks.rationale: An effect that omits a value it reads runs with a stale closure, so it acts on old props or state without any error.
checks.expectation: Each effect lists every reactive value it reads; logic that must read the latest value without re-running the effect uses `useEffectEvent` (React 19.2), not a suppressed or emptied dependency array.
checks.violationSignal: An empty or partial dependency array, often under a suppression, whose effect reads props, state, or context that change.

checks.title: Effect dependencies are stable without the compiler
checks.rationale: An object or function created during render and listed as an effect dependency re-runs the effect on every render, re-subscribing or re-fetching in a loop.
checks.expectation: Without the React Compiler, objects and functions an effect depends on are created inside the effect, moved out of the component, or memoized with `useMemo` or `useCallback`. Not applicable when the compiler compiles every component.
checks.violationSignal: An effect dependency that is an object, array, or function created fresh on each render.

checks.title: Custom hooks encapsulate one concern
checks.rationale: A hook that bundles unrelated state or wraps a lifecycle (`useMount`) hides its dependencies and spreads one change across every caller.
checks.expectation: Each custom hook owns one concern behind a small, consistent return shape, and is named for what it does rather than when it runs. Soft check — mixed adherence is reported as partial.
checks.violationSignal: Hooks that mix unrelated concerns, return inconsistent shapes, or exist only to run code on mount or update.

checks.title: Each value has one source of truth
checks.rationale: The same value held in two places, such as local state copied from a prop, a store, or the URL, goes out of sync and the screen shows contradictory data.
checks.expectation: Within a component tree, each value lives in one place and is derived or read everywhere else; a prop is not copied into state unless it is an explicitly named initial value.
checks.violationSignal: State initialised from a prop and then kept in sync, the same value held in two state variables, or local state mirroring a store or the URL.

checks.title: One status value instead of boolean flags
checks.rationale: Separate loading, error, and success booleans allow impossible combinations, such as a spinner and an error at once.
checks.expectation: A component that tracks a multi-step process holds one status value (`'idle' | 'loading' | 'success' | 'error'`) or uses the data layer's or `useActionState`'s state.
checks.violationSignal: Three or more boolean state variables that describe one process.

checks.title: State lives at the right level
checks.rationale: State held too high re-renders and couples unrelated screens; state held too low is duplicated or lost when a sibling needs it.
checks.expectation: Local state lives in the component that uses it, shared state at the lowest common parent, and global state only for application-wide concerns; hidden UI that must keep its state uses `<Activity>` or stays mounted. Soft check — mixed adherence is reported as partial.
checks.violationSignal: A global store or context holding one subtree's state, or state lifted far above the components that read it.

checks.title: Shareable view state lives in the URL
checks.rationale: Filters, sort orders, pages, and tabs held only in component state are lost on reload and cannot be shared as a link.
checks.expectation: View state a user would expect to survive a reload or a shared link lives in URL search parameters, through the router or a URL-state library. Soft check — mixed adherence is reported as partial.
checks.violationSignal: List filters, search queries, pagination, or selected tabs held only in `useState`.

checks.title: Components take ref as a prop
checks.rationale: React 19 passes `ref` as an ordinary prop and plans to deprecate forwardRef, so new wrappers add a legacy layer for nothing.
checks.expectation: In packages that require React 19, components accept `ref` as a prop; forwardRef remains only where a package's peer range still supports React 18. Not applicable below React 19.

checks.title: Components use named exports outside framework files
checks.rationale: A default-exported component is imported under any name, so renames and searches miss its uses.
checks.expectation: Component files export by name, except where the framework or loader requires a default export: Next.js pages, layouts, and other App Router files, Pages Router pages, React Router and Remix route modules, Expo Router routes, Gatsby pages, and React.lazy or next/dynamic targets.

checks.title: Forms submit through actions
checks.rationale: Hand-rolled submit handlers with their own pending and error state double-submit, lose errors, and drift from the server's response.
checks.expectation: On React 19, mutations from forms use form actions with `useActionState`, `useFormStatus`, and `useOptimistic` (or a form library that integrates them), so pending, error, and optimistic state come from one place. Not applicable below React 19.
checks.violationSignal: Forms that call `fetch` from `onSubmit` with separate `isSubmitting` and error state, or hand-rolled optimistic updates.

checks.title: Client modules import no server-only code
checks.rationale: A module reachable from a 'use client' file is bundled for the browser, so server code there either breaks the build or runs where its secrets are undefined.
checks.expectation: No module reachable through runtime imports from a 'use client' file imports `server-only`, a Node built-in, a database or server SDK, or reads a private environment variable; Server Functions are imported from 'use server' modules. Not applicable without React Server Components.
checks.violationSignal: A client module, or a module it imports, that imports server-only code or reads a private environment variable.

checks.title: Only serialisable props cross into client components
checks.rationale: A Server Component that passes a function or class instance to a client component fails at render, and a whole record passed down ships every field to the browser.
checks.expectation: Props from a Server Component to a client component are serialisable (plain data, Dates, Maps, Sets, Promises, JSX, or Server Functions) and selected field by field. Not applicable without React Server Components.
checks.violationSignal: A Server Component passing a plain function, class instance, or unshaped database record to a client component.

checks.title: 'use client' marks small interactive leaves
checks.rationale: A 'use client' directive high in the tree moves every module below it into the browser bundle and gives up server rendering for static content.
checks.expectation: 'use client' sits at the top of files that need state, effects, or browser APIs, as close to the leaves as possible, and never on a root layout or page; a misplaced directive below imports is moved to the first line. Not applicable without React Server Components.
checks.violationSignal: 'use client' on layouts, pages, or large containers that are mostly static, or a directive React ignores because it is not the first statement.
